subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `direct.<peer>.tools` and `toolsBySender` be an enforced per-DM-user security boundary, or should OpenClaw remove/diagnose that accepted config surface as unsupported?
rationale: The current schema has already shipped an apparently security-relevant config surface, but choosing enforcement semantics versus removal/diagnosis affects user security expectations, config compatibility, and policy precedence.

options.title: Enforce direct-message policy
options.body: Implement a direct/DM-aware policy path that preserves exact/wildcard/account/topic/sender precedence and add source plus live Telegram proof.

options.title: Deprecate the direct policy surface
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged but add a doctor migration or diagnostic plus docs that explain `direct.*.tools` is not supported.

options.title: Fold into broader binding policy design
options.body: Block this on a larger conversation-policy contract if maintainers want one unified policy model instead of a Telegram-specific repair.

recommendation.title: Enforce direct-message policy
recommendation.body: Implement a direct/DM-aware policy path that preserves exact/wildcard/account/topic/sender precedence and add source plus live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent scoped tool-policy work makes this the closest current security-boundary decision owner among the traced files.
